@graph.name: Cascade Bridge Adapter profile
@graph.description: An RO-Crate 1.2 Profile Crate for a Cascade Bridge Adapter. An adapter package is itself an RO-Crate whose root entity is the adapter; this profile is what that crate names in conformsTo to declare that it follows the Cascade Bridge Specification, and its constraints resource is the SHACL shapes shapes/bridge.shapes.ttl in the cascade-bridge-spec repository, which an adapter's crate and its test manifest are validated against as one graph. The profile IRI is https://ns.cascadeprotocol.org/bridge/v1-draft/adapter-profile/; it does not dereference yet, and until it does the specification is read from the repository. DRAFT: no compatibility is promised before a numbered v1. Two things about this file are the RO-Crate 1.2 validator's requirements rather than the specification's, and are recorded here so neither reads as a decision. The shapes and the vocabulary are named as web-based data entities, by their https://github.com/jayostis/cascade-bridge-spec/... URLs, because a data entity's @id must resolve inside the crate root and these files are outside it. And the profile IRI is carried as identifier on the root entity rather than as the root entity's own @id, because a crate's root entity @id is the crate directory, ./; a reader follows identifier to the profile IRI and conformsTo on an adapter's crate to the same string.

@graph.name: Cascade Bridge shapes
@graph.description: The constraints resource of this profile: SHACL shapes for an adapter's RO-Crate root entity and envelopes and for its test manifest, validated together as one graph with each file's own location as base. Requires a SHACL engine that supports SHACL-SPARQL. In the repository at shapes/bridge.shapes.ttl.

@graph.name: Cascade Bridge vocabulary
@graph.description: The bridge: vocabulary, https://ns.cascadeprotocol.org/bridge/v1-draft#: the adapter terms an adapter's crate root entity and envelopes use, and the test terms its test manifest uses on top of W3C's mf: test-manifest vocabulary. In the repository at vocab/bridge.ttl.
